newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - Aug 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - Aug 15.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Sri Lankan political and business stories prepared for Reuters by NewsWatch, Colombo Tel/Fax: 94-1-735182 Internet: lucien@eureka.lk.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Government plans to utilise loans from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) to upgrade certain industries, officials said. The ADB will provide an interest free loan of 1,180 million rupees ($ 20 million), while OPEC has pledged a 437 million rupees ($ 7.4 million) loan at concessionary term. The industries targetted are electronics, information technology, manufacturing engineering, biotechnology, aquaculture, environmental technology, polymer sciences, textiles and ready made garments.
BUS STRIKE CONTINUES IN SOME DEPOTS

Workers at 35 of the 93 bus depots, did not resume services on Thursday following harassment by unidentified persons. Government says it is not possible to grant demands for salary increases, as 70 percent of the depots that were handed over to the employees in early 1990s to generate large profits, are running at a loss.
PRESIDENT'S RESIDENCE TO BE SHIFTED DUE TO THREATS

Government says security threats prompted plans to shift the presidential residence from the capital Colombo to a Sri Jayawardenapura Kotte, a city suburb. Military experts from America, France and India had repeatedly warned about the high risk to the President living at Temple Trees in the capital, said Housing Minister Indika Gunawardene. The new presidential residence will be funded by the sale of 80 acres of land that presently houses several defence establishment in the capital.
NAVY DESTROYS FOUR TAMILO REBEL BOATS, KILLS 21 GUERRILLAS

Sri Lankan naval gunboats destroyed four Tamil rebel boats, killing more than 21 guerrillas in a confrontation at Pulmoddai on Thursday. The attack was made on a flotilla of 12 boats carrying rebels to a base on the northeastern coastal town of Mullaittivu. A naval gunboat was slightly damaged in the battle.
INDIA WILL NOT INTERFERE IN SRI LANKA'S WAR

India will not interfere in the war between the Sri Lankan army and the Tamil separatists, said Indian Prime Minister Gujral at the Indian Parliament on Thursday. He added that they had already burnt their fingers by interfering and that they would not do so again.
